title: How a Spider Builds Its Web in One Night
board: An empty page at dusk: two twigs, one spider
The gap: it lifts its abdomen, lets out silk
The thread drifts on the breeze
It snags; the spider walks the bridge
Stronger than steel, weight for weight; 7 silks
Dry spokes: where the spider walks
The sticky spiral, beaded with glue
Why it never sticks: branching hairs
Waiting at the hub, feeling the threads
Dawn: dew on every sticky thread
It eats the web, recycling the silk
